data.narrative:
Sphere Semi is a Seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised $20M to date. The founding team combines deep domain expertise: CEO Steven Glinert brings multi-stage startup experience and economics training, while CTO Mitchell Nahmias holds a Princeton PhD in photonic integrated circuits and co-founded Luminous Computing. The Chips & Semiconductors sector contains 11 private peers total, including later-stage companies such as Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched, alongside three public comparables (NVDA, AMD, ALAB).

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression analysis. Using total capital raised ($20M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier for progression from Seed to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $50M. This represents the most directly defensible anchor given the absence of sufficient same-stage or narrow peer data in the semiconductor space. A peer-median approach was inapplicable; while 11 same-sector peers exist, none of the tighter filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier) produced three or more comparable datapoints.

The triangulated valuation range is $42M–$57M, with a median of $50M. This range reflects the inherent uncertainty of single-method reliance and the early-stage nature of the company. Key unknowns include product-market validation, IP defensibility in photonic semiconductors, and the path to revenue. Given the nascency, material downside risk exists if technical milestones or fundraising timelines slip materially.
